title: Auth telemetry & operator-escrow: scope clarifications, rollout controls, and sign-off checklist
creator: Aisha Park
description: This ticket consolidates open questions and final acceptance criteria for two closely linked security subsystems for Private deployments: (1) auth telemetry (detailed SSO/SAML event capture, RBAC decision tracing, telemetry sampling and PII redaction) and (2) operator-escrow/KMS operator flows (HSM quorum, operator access escrow, rotation procedures). The objective is a tight, testable sign-off checklist that operations, product security, and legal can validate prior to GA onboarding for regulated customers.
scope_clarifications: Auth telemetry shall capture SAML assertion lifecycle events: assertion-issued, assertion-validated, assertion-expired, replay-detected (no raw PII such as full email addresses stored)
RBAC decision tracing must include: actor id, evaluated policy version, resource id, decision (allow/deny), decision-reason code, and request UUID for traceability
Audit log retention default: 365 days in customer-managed S3 (configurable to 7 years), with immutability flag for compliance customers

KMS/HSM operator-escrow: operators may store recovery keys in escrow vault with 2-of-3 HSM operator quorum required to release (configurable per-customer), and escrow access must be logged with tamper-evident proof
Rotation windows: automated key rotation every 90 days for non-customer-managed keys; supported manual rotation path for customer-managed keys with a documented rollback plan
Telemetry sampling: default 10% of token-level traces, 100% of SSO auth events; customer can opt to increase/decrease sample rate via Console
PII handling: telemetry pipeline will tokenize and redact email/local-part/hash identifiers before persisting to analytics buckets
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end SAML sign-in flow exercise demonstrates the expected telemetry events are emitted and persisted to the customer-configured audit sink (Conftest + sample logs attached)
RBAC policy change creates a versioned artifact; a simulated request shows the trace includes policy version and decision reason; Console shows policy-change diff in rollout UI
Audit logs exported to S3 are in JSONL format with schema v1.2 and pass schema validation and immutability tests (sha256 checksums verified)
KMS operator-escrow release is tested with a 2-of-3 HSM operator quorum in a staging cluster; release steps and telemetry for escrow actions recorded and reviewed
Key rotation smoke test completes without service interruption for a sample model endpoint and shows KV cache invalidation and graceful warm-up
Security review completed by Product Security and Legal with sign-off recorded in the signoff checklist and linked evidence
Ops runbook and playbooks for incident scenarios (stolen operator credentials, failed quorum) are published and validated in tabletop exercises
Performance regression < 5% p50 latency increase on a standard chat workload when auth telemetry enabled at default sampling
signoff_checklist: Security review ticket created and assigned to Product Security (link in artifacts)
Telemetry schema v1.2 validated against sample SAML events and RBAC traces
Console UI exposes telemetry sampling toggle and audit-sink configuration
RBAC policy versioning and rollout UI tested in Canary (A/B rollout success criteria met)
Escrow operator release tested with 3 HSM nodes; quorum behavior documented
Key rotation runbook, rollback steps, and post-rotation validation checklist published
Legal reviewed audit retention, immutability guarantees, and customer opt-in language
Customer onboarding checklist updated with new telemetry consent and KMS options
Automated acceptance tests added to CI that assert presence/format of telemetry events (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/8421)
Postmortem and lessons-learned template ready for any production escrow or rotation incident
decisions: Decision 2025-02-15: Default telemetry sampling will be conservative (10%) to limit egress costs; customers can enable full sampling for auth events
Decision 2025-02-17: Use JSONL schema v1.2 for audit exports to balance queryability and storage costs
Decision 2025-02-18: Operator-escrow will use HSM-backed sealed blobs with a configurable quorum; we will not ship plaintext escrow to object stores
Trade-off: Capturing richer traces increases cost and privacy exposure; chosen approach emphasizes structured, redacted telemetry and customer-configurable sampling
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Draft PRD published to Confluence (link below) with initial scope. Tagged Product Security for early feedback.
2025-02-14: Product Security requested stronger PII redaction controls and a default shorter retention for telemetry. Incorporated into scope.
2025-02-16: Engineering prototyped HSM operator-escrow flow in staging cluster; initial demo successful. Noted need for better replay-detection metrics.
2025-02-19: Legal confirmed acceptable retention ranges for EU customers and requested explicit consent language for audit export activation.
2025-02-20: QA added acceptance tests for RBAC decision trace, telemetry schema validation, and KMS rotation smoke tests. Preparing signoff meeting materials.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Telemetry enabled at high sampling could increase customer egress and storage costs. Mitigation: sampling configurable and capped; cost-estimator shown in Console.
Risk: Escrow release could be abused if operator credentials compromised. Mitigation: strict operator RBAC, multi-party quorum, and mandatory approval workflow logged with tamper-evident proofs.
Risk: Audit integrity requirement for compliance customers. Mitigation: immutable S3 objects + checksum verification + periodic attestation runs
next_steps: Hold cross-functional signoff review meeting (invite Product Security, Legal, Eng, Solutions) — target 2025-02-24
Merge acceptance-test PR and enable nightly runs against staging cluster
Publish customer-facing docs and onboarding checklist once sign-off complete
Schedule 1st customer pilot with two compliance-focused customers and track telemetry/costs
